lines.trans: When you cannot solve some problem, you only have one way out.
To forget it forever and
try to live on.
Defendant Denis Andreyevich Krylov, you are accused of infidelity.
But it is not my fault!
Right now it is going to get even better.
Arousal denied.
My stomach cramped up.
I need the toilet, it is a total nightmare in there.
Could you not hold it for at least an hour?
At least five minutes.
When our partners are not home, we will be running to the toilet like this all night.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.
Oh yeah? When?

examples.text: Правда? Когда вы не ели мясо?
examples.trans: Really? When did you not eat meat?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some kind of, some', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What nonsense.
Some man called you.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Borrowed via Polish/German from Greek 'problema' (something thrown forward, a task or question).

examples.trans: That's not a problem.
I have a problem.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ой, кажется, у вас сломан нос!
examples.trans: Oh, it looks like your nose is broken!

examples.text: Завтра у меня важное собеседование на работу.
examples.trans: Tomorrow I have an important job interview.

examples.text: Значит, у нас с тобой много общего.
examples.trans: So you and I have a lot in common.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was only looking.
Just one.
I was only looking!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
I have one brother.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'exit, way out' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There's always a way out.
Where is the exit?

examples.text: Как говорит наш губернатор, выход всегда есть.
examples.trans: As our governor says, there's always a way out.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.
I forgot the keys.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She's a lecturer.
I haven't heard of her.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'всегда').

examples.trans: Leave this place forever!
They parted forever.
Say that you are leaving for good.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пытаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try / attempt'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и попытаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to try on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют попытаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to to try.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.
I want to live normally.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'further, on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right. Next.
What's next?

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'судимый'). Common masculine noun meaning 'defendant' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The defendant stood up.
The defendant's health.

examples.text: Конфликты с соседями угрожают здоровью подсудимого.
examples.trans: Conflicts with the neighbours threaten the defendant's health.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'Krylov' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть крылов.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always Krylov.
The chef immediately noticed where the Krylov was.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'Andreyevich' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть андреевич.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always Andreyevich.
The chef immediately noticed where the Andreyevich was.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'виняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'you are accused'.

related.gloss: not to you are accused (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и обвиняться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and you are accused on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют обвиняться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to you are accused.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'мена'). Common feminine noun meaning 'infidelity / treason' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть измена.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always infidelity.
The chef immediately noticed where the infidelity was.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('at fault, guilty').

examples.trans: It's your fault!

examples.text: Я ни в чём не виноват.
examples.trans: I'm not to blame for anything.
I know it's my fault.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'still', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It's better like this.
I feel better today.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'збуждение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'initiation / arousal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть возбуждение.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always initiation.
The chef immediately noticed where the initiation was.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to refuse / deny', paired with 'отказывать'.

examples.text: Марина, послушайте, это я вам отказал!
examples.trans: Marina, listen, I was the one who turned you down!
They turned him down in court.

examples.text: Я мерзкий? Марина, послушайте, это я вам отказал!
examples.trans: I'm disgusting? Marina, listen, I was the one who turned you down!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'belly' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He has a big belly.
My stomach hurts.

examples.text: Живот у тебя, как у депутата.
examples.trans: You've got a belly like a member of parliament.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'хватить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'seized / cramped up'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и прихватить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and seized on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют прихватить.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to seized.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'restroom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Where's the toilet?
The toilet is in the corridor.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'hanger / total nightmare' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть вешалка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always hanger.
The chef immediately noticed where the hanger was.

meanings.en: to be patient for a little while, to hold on
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терпеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hold on / endure', paired with 'терпеть'.

examples.text: Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: We need to be patient a little and work a bit.
Hang on for five more minutes.

examples.text: Послушай меня, Ваня. Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: Listen to me, Vanya. We need to be patient a little and work a bit.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Хочу хотя бы один спокойный день!
examples.trans: I want at least one calm day!
Then you will have at least tried.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, выслушайте меня хотя бы минуту.
examples.trans: Please, listen to me for at least a minute.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I would think about it.
I'd buy a house.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'an hour or so' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть часик.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always an hour or so.
The chef immediately noticed where the an hour or so was.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minutes' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.
Just a minute!

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'five', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Five thousand roubles.
I'm five years old.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ожитель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of roommates / partners' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть сожитель.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always of roommates.
The chef immediately noticed where the of roommates was.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'at home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, you keep him at home.
Today I'm staying at home.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А то, что между нами было?
examples.trans: What about what was between us?

examples.text: Не задавай глупых вопросов, а то передумаю!
examples.trans: Do not ask foolish questions, or I'll change my mind!

examples.text: Это именно то, о чём я мечтал!
examples.trans: This is exactly what I dreamed about!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.en: to run (in various directions or habitually)
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to run back and forth', paired with 'побежать'.

examples.trans: She was running after me.
The children are running around in the yard.

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Вокруг меня бегала.
examples.trans: She was the one who came up to me! She was running after me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'entire', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'night' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Good night!
At night I sleep.

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.
